A1.justification: Both PDFs describe the same 2HandedAfforder work. Their main text, tables, figures and complete supplementary Sections 7–12 are readable and can be matched reliably despite pagination changes.

before.justification: v1 reports original ActAffordance benchmark results in Table 2, robot demonstrations, and qualitative failure and mask-completion analyses.

after.justification: v3 retains the original quantitative evaluations and robot experiments and adds qualitative baseline predictions in Figure 5.

M1.justification: The affordance extraction pipeline, VLM/SAM architecture, separate hand decoders, taxonomy head, LoRA training, losses and CLIP alternative remain unchanged. Additional explanations do not introduce a different procedure.

E1.justification: Both versions use EPIC-KITCHENS/VISOR for 2HANDS, EPIC-KITCHENS and Ego4D for full and cropped ActAffordance evaluation, and the same kitchen robot tasks. Newly cited datasets are not added to the experiments.

E2.justification: Figure 5 adds LOCATE and VRB to the qualitative comparison alongside LISA, AffordanceLLM and 3DOI. LOCATE and VRB already appeared in v1's quantitative evaluations; Table 2's comparator membership is unchanged.

E3.justification: The benchmark splits, 400 activities, 10 annotators, metrics, threshold aggregation and robot setup are retained. Section 5.2 newly documents baseline mask matching and input prompts without establishing a revision to the existing evaluation protocol.

E4.justification: Figure 5 extends the qualitative examination of region localization on three existing tasks with LOCATE and VRB predictions. This modestly expands the case comparison; the dedicated failure cases, robot comparisons and mask-completion analysis in the appendix remain unchanged.

E5.justification: Neither version reports experimental seed counts, repeated-run variability, confidence intervals or significance tests. Table 2 retains the same averaging over five prediction thresholds, which is not repeated-run uncertainty reporting.

E6.justification: Figure 5 adds six qualitative predictions from LOCATE and VRB. All Table 2 numerical entries remain identical, including 2HandedAfforder's combined precision of 0.130 on the full benchmark and 0.269 on the cropped benchmark.

T1.justification: The loss descriptions and Hausdorff-distance explanations retain their mathematical content. Neither version contains a theoretical result or proof that is added, removed or revised.

C1.justification: The principal contributions remain video-derived precise bimanual affordances, 2HANDS, 2HandedAfforder, ActAffordance and robotic actionability. Rewording the benchmark contribution and shortening the conclusion do not materially change these claims.

C2.justification: Section 5.2 newly argues that comparisons with architecturally similar LISA and AffordanceLLM help isolate the dataset's contribution, while stating that baselines cannot be trained on 2HANDS. Existing explanations of errors and failure conditions are retained.

D1.justification: v3 specifies union-of-hand-mask evaluation for LISA, LOCATE and AffordanceLLM, and ground-truth bounding-box/object-center inputs for VRB and 3DOI. Appendix Section 8 adds a prospective dataset and code release statement at the existing project website; actual release is not established by the PDFs.

R1.justification: v3 adds HRP, GigaHands and TACO to the related-work citations, expanding acknowledgment of affordance and bimanual research. The central novelty positioning remains unchanged.

P1.justification: Localized edits clarify benchmark motivation, metrics and baseline evaluation, add a Section 3 overview, and shorten the conclusion by removing its final robot-summary and future-work sentences. Appendix figure references are corrected; the section organization remains intact.

P2.justification: Figure 5 gains two baseline rows and moves to the left column. Figure 3 mirrors the chopping example and adjusts token-label styling. Captions, spacing and pagination also change, while the remaining figures and table structures are substantially retained.

improvement.justification: The explicit baseline evaluation details, expanded Figure 5 and corrected appendix references make the existing evidence easier to assess. These are limited gains: quantitative validation is unchanged, code/data release remains prospective, and the new dataset-effect interpretation lacks a controlled dataset ablation.
